title: The Frog Prince
blurb: A princess drops her golden ball. A frog makes her promise.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… when wishing still helped, there was a King whose daughters were all beautiful — [gently] but the youngest was so beautiful that even the sun, who has seen everything, was surprised whenever it shone on her face.

[playfully] Near the castle there was a dark wood, and in the wood a cool well. [excited] And when the day was hot, the young Princess would sit by that well and play with a golden ball, throwing it up and catching it.

[worried] One day the ball went a little too high. [surprised] It slipped past her hands, bounced once on the stone… [short pause] and fell into the water.

[sad] She leaned over and looked. The well was deep. So deep that she could not see the bottom.

[crying] And the Princess began to cry.

[curious] Then a voice said, “What is the matter?”

[surprised] She looked round. [amused] And there, poking his fat ugly head out of the water, was a Frog.

[sad] “My golden ball has fallen in,” she said.

[calmly] “I can fetch it,” said the Frog. “But what will you give me?”

[excited] “Anything!” she said. “My pearls, my jewels, my golden crown.”

[thoughtful] “I do not want your pearls,” said the Frog. [gently] “But if you will love me, and let me be your companion — let me sit at your table, and eat from your little plate, and drink from your little cup, and sleep in your little bed — [firmly] then I will dive down and fetch your ball.”

[amused] “Oh yes! Anything!” said the Princess. [whispers] But she thought to herself, what nonsense. A frog cannot leave the water. He can be nobody's companion.

[excited] So the Frog dived, and came up with the golden ball in his mouth, and dropped it on the grass.

[happy] The Princess snatched it up and ran.

[worried] “Wait!” cried the Frog. “Take me with you! I cannot run as you can!” [sad] But she did not listen, and she did not look back. [short pause] And soon she had forgotten him altogether.

[calmly] But the next evening, as the family sat at dinner, something came flopping up the marble stairs. [short pause] Splash. Splash. Splash.

[worried] It knocked at the door. [whispers] “Youngest daughter, open to me.”

[surprised] She opened the door, saw the Frog, and slammed it shut again.

[firmly] “What is it?” said the King. And she told him.

[gently] “Then you must keep your promise,” said her father. “What you have promised, you must do. Go and let him in.”

[sad] So the Frog came in. He sat at the table. He ate from her little plate. [annoyed] And she did not like it one bit.

And when he asked to be carried upstairs, she was so upset that she picked him up and put him down hard on the pillow.

[surprised] And in that moment, the Frog was a frog no longer. [excited] There stood a young Prince, with kind eyes — [warmly] freed at last from a spell, by a promise that was kept.
